74:  * Description:
75:  *   This is a primitive counting synchronization mechanism

78:  * Input Parameters:
79:  *   seqcount_t

81:  * Returned Value:
82:  *   seq - Used to determine whether the state has changed during reading.

87: uint32_t read_seqbegin(FAR const seqcount_t *s)
88: {

91: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
92:   seq = atomic_read_acquire(&s->sequence) & ~1;
93: #else
94:   seq = s->sequence;
95:   SMP_RMB();
96: #endif
97:   return seq;
98: }

101:  * Name: read_seqretry
102:  *
103:  * Description:
104:  *   This is a primitive counting synchronization mechanism
105:  *   that enables lock-free reading.
106:  *
107:  * Input Parameters:
108:  *   seqcount_t
109:  *   start - Used to determine whether the state has changed during reading.
110:  *
111:  * Returned Value:

113:  *
114:  ****************************************************************************/

116: static inline_function
117: uint32_t read_seqretry(FAR const seqcount_t *s, uint32_t start)
118: {
119:   uint32_t seq;
120: 
121:   /* Ensure all load operations before are completed. */
122: 
123:   SMP_RMB();
124: 
125: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
126:   seq = atomic_read(&s->sequence);
127: #else
128:   seq = s->sequence;
129: #endif

140:  *
141:  * Input Parameters:

143:  *
144:  * Returned Value:
145:  *   irqstate

147:  ****************************************************************************/

151: {

153: 
154: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
155:   for (; ; )
156:     {
157:       uint32_t sequence = atomic_read(&s->sequence);

160:         {
161:           /* Try to acquire the lock ownership. */
162: 
163:           if (atomic_cmpxchg_acquire(&s->sequence, &sequence, sequence + 1u))
164:             {
165:               break;
166:             }
167:         }
168: 
169:       /* CPU Relax and retry. */
170:     }
171: #else
172:   s->sequence++;
173: #endif
174: 
175:   return flags;
176: }

52: /****************************************************************************
53:  * Name:  nxsched_cpu_scheduler
54:  *
55:  * Description:
56:  *   Check for operations specific to scheduling policy of the currently
57:  *   active task on one CPU.
58:  *
59:  * Input Parameters:
60:  *   cpu - The CPU that we are performing the scheduler operations on.
61:  *
62:  * Returned Value:
63:  *   None
64:  *
65:  ****************************************************************************/
66: 
67: #if CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL > 0 || defined(CONFIG_SCHED_SPORADIC)
68: static inline void nxsched_cpu_scheduler(int cpu)
69: {
70:   FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = current_task(cpu);
71: 
72: #if CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL > 0
73:   /* Check if the currently executing task uses round robin scheduling. */
74: 
75:   if ((atomic_read(&rtcb->flags) & TCB_FLAG_POLICY_MASK) ==
76:       TCB_FLAG_SCHED_RR)
77:     {
78:       /* Yes, check if the currently executing task has exceeded its
79:        * timeslice.
80:        */
81: 
82:       nxsched_process_roundrobin(rtcb, 1, false);
83:     }
84: #endif
85: 
86: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_SPORADIC
87:   /* Check if the currently executing task uses sporadic scheduling. */
88: 
89:   if ((atomic_read(&rtcb->flags) & TCB_FLAG_POLICY_MASK) ==
90:       TCB_FLAG_SCHED_SPORADIC)
91:     {
92:       /* Yes, check if the currently executing task has exceeded its
93:        * budget.
94:        */
95: 
96:       nxsched_process_sporadic(rtcb, 1, false);
97:     }
98: #endif
99: }
100: #endif
101: 
102: /****************************************************************************
103:  * Name:  nxsched_process_scheduler
104:  *
105:  * Description:
106:  *   Check for operations specific to scheduling policy of the currently
107:  *   active task on all configured CPUs.
108:  *
109:  * Input Parameters:
110:  *   None
111:  *
112:  * Returned Value:
113:  *   None
114:  *
115:  ****************************************************************************/
116: 
117: #if CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL > 0 || defined(CONFIG_SCHED_SPORADIC)
118: static inline void nxsched_process_scheduler(void)
119: {
120:   irqstate_t flags;
121:   int i;
122: 
123:   /* Single CPU case:
124:    * For nested interrupts, higher IRQs may interrupt nxsched_cpu_scheduler()
125:    * but nxsched_cpu_scheduler() requires that interrupts be disabled.
126:    * We are in ISR context, no meaning we are disabled the interrupts.
127:    *
128:    * SMP case:
129:    * enter_critical_section() does much more than just disable interrupts on
130:    * the local CPU; it also manages spinlocks to assure the stability of the
131:    * TCB that we are manipulating.
132:    */
133: 
134:   flags = enter_critical_section();
135: 
136:   /* Perform scheduler operations on all CPUs */
137: 
138:   for (i = 0; i < CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS; i++)
139:     {
140:       nxsched_cpu_scheduler(i);
141:     }
142: 
143:   leave_critical_section(flags);
144: }
145: #else
146: #  define nxsched_process_scheduler()
147: #endif
148: 
149: /****************************************************************************
150:  * Public Functions
151:  ****************************************************************************/
152: 
153: /****************************************************************************
154:  * System Timer Hooks
155:  *
156:  * These are standard interfaces that are exported by the OS
157:  * for use by the architecture specific logic
158:  *
159:  ****************************************************************************/
160: 
161: /****************************************************************************
162:  * Name:  nxsched_process_timer
163:  *
164:  * Description:
165:  *   This function handles system timer events.
166:  *   The timer interrupt logic itself is implemented in the
167:  *   architecture specific code, but must call the following OS
168:  *   function periodically -- the calling interval must be
169:  *   USEC_PER_TICK
170:  *
171:  * Input Parameters:
172:  *   None
173:  *
174:  * Returned Value:
175:  *   None
176:  *
177:  ****************************************************************************/
178: 
179: void nxsched_process_timer(void)
180: {
181: #ifdef CONFIG_CLOCK_TIMEKEEPING
182:   /* Process wall time */
183: 
184:   clock_update_wall_time();
185: #endif
186: 
187:   /* Increment the system time (if in the link) */
188: 
189:   clock_timer();
190: 
191:   /* Check if the currently executing task has exceeded its
192:    * timeslice.
193:    */
194: 
195:   nxsched_process_scheduler();
196: 
197:   /* Process watchdogs */
198: 
199:   wd_timer(clock_systime_ticks());
200: 
201: #ifdef CONFIG_SYSTEMTICK_HOOK
202:   /* Call out to a user-provided function in order to perform board-specific,
203:    * custom timer operations.
204:    */
205: 
206:   board_timerhook();
207: #endif
208: }

87: /****************************************************************************
88:  * Name: clock_basetime
89:  *
90:  * Description:
91:  *   Get the initial time value from the best source available.
92:  *
93:  ****************************************************************************/
94: 
95: #ifdef CONFIG_RTC
96: #if defined(CONFIG_RTC_DATETIME)
97: /* Initialize the system time using a broken out date/time structure */
98: 
99: int clock_basetime(FAR struct timespec *tp)
100: {
101:   struct tm rtctime;
102:   long nsecs = 0;
103:   int ret;
104: 
105:   /* Get the broken-out time from the date/time RTC. */
106: 
107: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_HAVE_RTC_SUBSECONDS
108:   ret = up_rtc_getdatetime_with_subseconds(&rtctime, &nsecs);
109: #else
110:   ret = up_rtc_getdatetime(&rtctime);
111: #endif
112:   if (ret >= 0)
113:     {
114:       /* And use the broken-out time to initialize the system time */
115: 
116:       tp->tv_sec  = timegm(&rtctime);
117:       tp->tv_nsec = nsecs;
118:     }
119: 
120:   return ret;
121: }
122: 
123: #elif defined(CONFIG_RTC_HIRES)
124: 
125: /* Initialize the system time using a high-resolution structure */
126: 
127: int clock_basetime(FAR struct timespec *tp)
128: {
129:   /* Get the complete time from the hi-res RTC. */
130: 
131:   return up_rtc_gettime(tp);
132: }
133: 
134: #else
135: 
136: /* Initialize the system time using seconds only */
137: 
138: int clock_basetime(FAR struct timespec *tp)
139: {
140:   /* Get the seconds (only) from the lo-resolution RTC */
141: 
142:   tp->tv_sec  = up_rtc_time();
143:   tp->tv_nsec = 0;
144:   return OK;
145: }
146: 
147: #endif /* CONFIG_RTC_HIRES */
148: #else /* CONFIG_RTC */
149: 
150: int clock_basetime(FAR struct timespec *tp)
151: {
152:   time_t jdn = 0;
153: 
154:   /* Get the EPOCH-relative julian date from the calendar year,
155:    * month, and date
156:    */
157: 
158:   jdn = clock_calendar2utc(CONFIG_START_YEAR, CONFIG_START_MONTH - 1,
159:                            CONFIG_START_DAY);
160: 
161:   /* Set the base time as seconds into this julian day. */
162: 
163:   tp->tv_sec  = jdn * (time_t)SEC_PER_DAY;
164:   tp->tv_nsec = 0;
165:   return OK;
166: }
167: 
168: #endif /* CONFIG_RTC */

170: /****************************************************************************
171:  * Name: clock_inittime
172:  *
173:  * Description:
174:  *   Get the initial time value from the best source available.
175:  *
176:  ****************************************************************************/
177: 
178: #ifdef CONFIG_RTC
179: static void clock_inittime(FAR const struct timespec *tp)
180: {
181:   /* (Re-)initialize the time value to match the RTC */
182: 
183: #ifndef CONFIG_CLOCK_TIMEKEEPING
184:   struct timespec ts;
185:   irqstate_t flags;
186: 
187:   clock_systime_timespec(&ts);
188: 
189:   flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&g_basetime_lock);
190:   if (tp)
191:     {
192:       memcpy(&g_basetime, tp, sizeof(struct timespec));
193:     }
194:   else
195:     {
196:       clock_basetime(&g_basetime);
197:     }
198: 
199:   /* Adjust base time to hide initial timer ticks. */
200: 
201:   g_basetime.tv_sec  -= ts.tv_sec;
202:   g_basetime.tv_nsec -= ts.tv_nsec;
203:   while (g_basetime.tv_nsec < 0)
204:     {
205:       g_basetime.tv_nsec += NSEC_PER_SEC;
206:       g_basetime.tv_sec--;
207:     }
208: 
209:   spin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_basetime_lock, flags);
210:   clock_notifier_call_chain(CLOCK_REALTIME, &g_basetime);
211: #else
212:   clock_inittimekeeping(tp);
213: #endif
214: }
215: #endif

273:  *   initialization.  However, the user may also need to explicitly re-
274:  *   synchronize the system timer to the RTC under certain conditions where
275:  *   the system timer is known to be in error.  For example, in certain low-
276:  *   power states, the system timer may be stopped but the RTC will continue
277:  *   keep correct time.  After recovering from such low-power state, this
278:  *   function should be called to restore the correct system time.
279:  *
280:  *   Calling this function could result in system time going "backward" in
281:  *   time, especially with certain lower resolution RTC implementations.
282:  *   Time going backward could have bad consequences if there are ongoing
283:  *   timers and delays.  So use this interface with care.
284:  *
285:  * Input Parameters:

326:   /* Re-initialize the time value to match the RTC */
327: 
328:   flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&g_basetime_lock);
329: 
330:   clock_systime_timespec(&ts);
331:   g_monotonic_basetime.tv_sec = tp->tv_sec - ts.tv_sec;
332:   g_monotonic_basetime.tv_nsec = tp->tv_nsec - ts.tv_nsec;
333:   if (g_monotonic_basetime.tv_nsec < 0)
334:     {
335:       g_monotonic_basetime.tv_sec -= 1;
336:       g_monotonic_basetime.tv_nsec += NSEC_PER_SEC;
337:     }
338: 
339:   spin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_basetime_lock, flags);
340: }
341: #endif
342: 
343: /****************************************************************************
344:  * Name: clock_resynchronize
345:  *
346:  * Description:
347:  *   Resynchronize the system timer to a hardware RTC.  The user can
348:  *   explicitly re-synchronize the system timer to the RTC under certain
349:  *   conditions where the system timer is known to be in error.  For example,
350:  *   in certain low-power states, the system timer may be stopped but the
351:  *   RTC will continue keep correct time.  After recovering from such
352:  *   low-power state, this function should be called to restore the correct
353:  *   system time. Function also keeps monotonic clock at rate of RTC.
354:  *
355:  *   Calling this function will not result in system time going "backward" in
356:  *   time. If setting system time with RTC would result time going "backward"
357:  *   then resynchronization is not performed.
358:  *
359:  * Input Parameters:
360:  *   rtc_diff:  amount of time system-time is adjusted forward with RTC
361:  *
362:  * Returned Value:
363:  *   None
364:  *
365:  * Assumptions:
366:  *
367:  ****************************************************************************/
368: 
369: #if defined(CONFIG_RTC) && !defined(CONFIG_SCHED_TICKLESS) && \
370:     !defined(CONFIG_CLOCK_TIMEKEEPING) && !defined(CONFIG_ALARM_ARCH) && \
371:     !defined(CONFIG_TIMER_ARCH)
372: void clock_resynchronize(FAR struct timespec *rtc_diff)
373: {
374:   struct timespec rtc_time;
375:   struct timespec bias;
376:   struct timespec curr_ts;
377:   struct timespec rtc_diff_tmp;
378:   irqstate_t flags;
379:   int ret;
380: 
381:   if (rtc_diff == NULL)
382:     {
383:       rtc_diff = &rtc_diff_tmp;
384:     }
385: 
386:   /* Get RTC time */
387: 
388:   ret = clock_basetime(&rtc_time);
389:   if (ret < 0)
390:     {
391:       /* Error reading RTC, skip resynchronization. */
392: 
393:       sinfo("rtc error %d, skip resync\n", ret);
394: 
395:       rtc_diff->tv_sec = 0;
396:       rtc_diff->tv_nsec = 0;
397:       return;
398:     }
399: 
400:   /* Set the time value to match the RTC */
401: 
402:   /* Get the elapsed time since power up (in milliseconds).  This is a
403:    * bias value that we need to use to correct the base time.
404:    */
405: 
406:   clock_systime_timespec(&bias);
407: 
408:   /* Add the base time to this.  The base time is the time-of-day
409:    * setting.  When added to the elapsed time since the time-of-day
410:    * was last set, this gives us the current time.
411:    */
412: 
413:   flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&g_basetime_lock);
414:   clock_timespec_add(&bias, &g_basetime, &curr_ts);
415:   spin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_basetime_lock, flags);
416: 
417:   /* Check if RTC has advanced past system time. */
418: 
419:   if (curr_ts.tv_sec > rtc_time.tv_sec ||
420:       (curr_ts.tv_sec == rtc_time.tv_sec &&
421:        curr_ts.tv_nsec >= rtc_time.tv_nsec))
422:     {
423:       /* Setting system time with RTC now would result time going
424:        * backwards. Skip resynchronization.
425:        */
426: 
427:       sinfo("skip resync\n");
428: 
429:       rtc_diff->tv_sec = 0;
430:       rtc_diff->tv_nsec = 0;
431:     }
432:   else
433:     {
434:       /* Output difference between time at entry and new current time. */
435: 
436:       clock_timespec_subtract(&rtc_time, &curr_ts, rtc_diff);
437: 
438:       /* Add the sleep time to correct system timer */
439: 
440:       clock_t diff_ticks = SEC2TICK(rtc_diff->tv_sec) +
441:                            NSEC2TICK(rtc_diff->tv_nsec);
442: 
443:       flags = write_seqlock_irqsave(&g_system_tick_lock);
444:       g_system_ticks += diff_ticks;
445:       write_sequnlock_irqrestore(&g_system_tick_lock, flags);
446:     }
447: }
448: #endif
449: 
450: /****************************************************************************
451:  * Name: clock_timer
452:  *
453:  * Description:
454:  *   This function must be called once every time the real time clock
455:  *   interrupt occurs.  The interval of this clock interrupt must be
456:  *   USEC_PER_TICK
457:  *
458:  ****************************************************************************/
459: 
460: #if !defined(CONFIG_SCHED_TICKLESS) && \
461:     !defined(CONFIG_ALARM_ARCH) && !defined(CONFIG_TIMER_ARCH)
462: void clock_timer(void)
463: {
464:   irqstate_t flags;
465: 
466:   /* Increment the per-tick system counter */
467: 
468:   flags = write_seqlock_irqsave(&g_system_tick_lock);
469:   g_system_ticks++;
470:   write_sequnlock_irqrestore(&g_system_tick_lock, flags);
471: }
472: #endif

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * BK7258 raw Mailbox SMP IPI.
3:  ****************************************************************************/
4: 
5: #include <nuttx/config.h>
6: 
7: #include <assert.h>
8: #include <errno.h>
9: #include <stdint.h>
10: #include <strings.h>
11: 
12: #include <nuttx/arch.h>
13: #include <nuttx/atomic.h>
14: #include <nuttx/sched.h>
15: 
16: #include "arm_internal.h"
17: #include "sched/sched.h"
18: #include "hardware/bk7258_mbox.h"
19: #include "bk7258_boottrace.h"
20: #include "bk7258_smp.h"
21: 
22: #define BK7258_IPI_SCHED        (1u << 0)
23: #define BK7258_IPI_CALL         (1u << 1)
24: #define BK7258_IPI_RETRY_LIMIT  1024
25: 
26: #define BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_NOTIFY (BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK + 1u)
27: #define BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_PING   (BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK + 2u)
28: #define BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_ACK    (BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK + 3u)
29: 
30: #define BK7258_BOOT_SEEN_NOTIFY (1u << 0)
31: #define BK7258_BOOT_SEEN_ACK    (1u << 1)
32: 
33: #define BK7258_IPI_TRACE_ENTRY  0xb1000000u
34: #define BK7258_IPI_TRACE_CLAIM  0xb2000000u
35: #define BK7258_IPI_TRACE_SENT   0xb3000000u
36: #define BK7258_IPI_TRACE_FAIL   0xb4000000u
37: 
38: static atomic_t g_ipi_pending[CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS];
39: static atomic_t g_ipi_kicked[CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS];
40: static atomic_t g_boot_ping_received;
41: static uint32_t g_boot_seen;
42: 
43: static void bk7258_smp_trace(uint32_t value)
44: {
45:   if (bk7258_boottrace_primary_stage() == BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_FIRST_IRQ)
46:     {
47:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(4, value);
48:     }
49: }
50: 
51: static int bk7258_smp_boot_send(int cpu, uint32_t command)
52: {
53:   uint32_t data[2] = {command, 0};
54:   int retry;
55: 
56:   UP_DMB();
57:   for (retry = 0; retry < BK7258_IPI_RETRY_LIMIT; retry++)
58:     {
59:       int ret = bk7258_mbox_send((uint8_t)(cpu + 1), data);
60: 
61:       if (ret == OK)
62:         {
63:           return OK;
64:         }
65: 
66:       if (ret != -EAGAIN)
67:         {
68:           return ret;
69:         }
70: 
71:       __asm__ volatile("nop");
72:     }
73: 
74:   return -ETIMEDOUT;
75: }
76: 
77: static int bk7258_smp_kick(int cpu, uint32_t pending)
78: {
79:   uint32_t data[2] = {BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK, 0};
80:   int expected = 0;
81:   int retry;
82: 
83:   if ((unsigned int)cpu >= CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS || cpu == this_cpu())
84:     {
85:       return -EINVAL;
86:     }
87: 
88:   bk7258_smp_trace(BK7258_IPI_TRACE_ENTRY | (pending & 0xffu));
89:   atomic_or_release(&g_ipi_pending[cpu], pending);
90:   if (!atomic_cmpxchg_acquire(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], &expected, 1))
91:     {
92:       bk7258_smp_trace(BK7258_IPI_TRACE_CLAIM | 0x100u);
93:       return OK;
94:     }
95: 
96:   bk7258_smp_trace(BK7258_IPI_TRACE_CLAIM | (cpu & 0xffu));
97:   UP_DMB();
98:   for (retry = 0; retry < BK7258_IPI_RETRY_LIMIT; retry++)
99:     {
100:       int ret = bk7258_mbox_send((uint8_t)(cpu + 1), data);
101: 
102:       if (ret == OK)
103:         {
104:           bk7258_smp_trace(BK7258_IPI_TRACE_SENT | (retry & 0xffffu));
105:           return OK;
106:         }
107: 
108:       if (ret != -EAGAIN)
109:         {
110:           atomic_set_release(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], 0);
111:           bk7258_smp_trace(BK7258_IPI_TRACE_FAIL |
112:                            ((uint32_t)(-ret) & 0xffffu));
113:           return ret;
114:         }
115: 
116:       __asm__ volatile("nop");
117:     }
118: 
119:   atomic_set_release(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], 0);
120:   bk7258_smp_trace(BK7258_IPI_TRACE_FAIL | 0xffffu);
121:   return -ETIMEDOUT;
122: }
123: 
124: void bk7258_smp_ipi_receive(int irq, void *context, uint32_t command)
125: {
126:   int cpu = this_cpu();
127: 
128:   if (command == BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_NOTIFY)
129:     {
130:       if (cpu == 0)
131:         {
132:           g_boot_seen |= BK7258_BOOT_SEEN_NOTIFY;
133:         }
134: 
135:       return;
136:     }
137: 
138:   if (command == BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_PING)
139:     {
140:       if (cpu == 1)
141:         {
142:           atomic_set_release(&g_boot_ping_received, 1);
143:           if (bk7258_boottrace_secondary_stage() <
144:               BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ACK)
145:             {
146:               bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ACK);
147:             }
148:         }
149: 
150:       return;
151:     }
152: 
153:   if (command == BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_ACK)
154:     {
155:       if (cpu == 0)
156:         {
157:           g_boot_seen |= BK7258_BOOT_SEEN_ACK;
158:         }
159: 
160:       return;
161:     }
162: 
163:   if (command != BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK)
164:     {
165:       return;
166:     }
167: 
168:   for (;;)
169:     {
170:       uint32_t pending = atomic_xchg_acquire(&g_ipi_pending[cpu], 0);
171: 
172:       if ((pending & BK7258_IPI_CALL) != 0)
173:         {
174:           nxsched_smp_call_handler(irq, context, NULL);
175:         }
176: 
177:       if ((pending & BK7258_IPI_SCHED) != 0)
178:         {
179:           nxsched_process_delivered(cpu);
180:         }
181: 
182:       atomic_set_release(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], 0);
183:       UP_DMB();
184:       if (atomic_read_acquire(&g_ipi_pending[cpu]) == 0)
185:         {
186:           break;
187:         }
188: 
189:       atomic_set_release(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], 1);
190:     }
191: }
192: 
193: int up_send_smp_sched(int cpu)
194: {
195:   int ret = bk7258_smp_kick(cpu, BK7258_IPI_SCHED);
196: 
197:   if (ret < 0)
198:     {
199:       return ret;
200:     }
201: 
202:   return ret;
203: }
204: 
205: void bk7258_smp_retry_pending(void)
206: {
207:   if (this_cpu() == 0 && atomic_read_acquire(&g_ipi_pending[1]) != 0 &&
208:       atomic_read_acquire(&g_ipi_kicked[1]) == 0)
209:     {
210:       (void)bk7258_smp_kick(1, 0);
211:     }
212: }
213: 
214: void up_send_smp_call(cpu_set_t cpuset)
215: {
216:   int cpu;
217: 
218:   for (; cpuset != 0; cpuset &= ~(1u << cpu))
219:     {
220:       cpu = ffs((int)cpuset) - 1;
221:       if (cpu != this_cpu() && bk7258_smp_kick(cpu, BK7258_IPI_CALL) < 0)
222:         {
223:           /* The pending call bit remains set for a later coalesced kick. */
224:         }
225:     }
226: }
227: 
228: void bk7258_smp_prepare_boot(void)
229: {
230:   int cpu;
231: 
232:   for (cpu = 0; cpu < CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS; cpu++)
233:     {
234:       atomic_set(&g_ipi_pending[cpu], 0);
235:       atomic_set(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], 0);
236:     }
237: 
238:   g_boot_seen = 0;
239:   atomic_set(&g_boot_ping_received, 0);
240:   UP_DMB();
241: }
242: 
243: void bk7258_smp_boot_notify(void)
244: {
245:   if (bk7258_smp_boot_send(0, BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_NOTIFY) < 0)
246:     {
247:       PANIC();
248:     }
249: }
250: 
251: void bk7258_smp_boot_ack(void)
252: {
253:   if (bk7258_smp_boot_send(0, BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_ACK) < 0)
254:     {
255:       PANIC();
256:     }
257: }
258: 
259: bool bk7258_smp_boot_notified(void)
260: {
261:   return (g_boot_seen & BK7258_BOOT_SEEN_NOTIFY) != 0;
262: }
263: 
264: bool bk7258_smp_boot_ping_received(void)
265: {
266:   return atomic_read_acquire(&g_boot_ping_received) != 0;
267: }
268: 
269: bool bk7258_smp_boot_test_complete(void)
270: {
271:   return g_boot_seen == (BK7258_BOOT_SEEN_NOTIFY |
272:                          BK7258_BOOT_SEEN_ACK);
273: }
274: 
275: int bk7258_smp_boot_ping(int cpu)
276: {
277:   return bk7258_smp_boot_send(cpu, BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_PING);
278: }

32: /****************************************************************************
33:  * Name: arm_fpuconfig
34:  *
35:  * Description:
36:  *   Configure the FPU.  Relative bit settings:
37:  *
38:  *     CPACR:  Enables access to CP10 and CP11
39:  *     CONTROL.FPCA: Determines whether the FP extension is active in the
40:  *       current context:
41:  *     FPCCR.ASPEN:  Enables automatic FP state preservation, then the
42:  *       processor sets this bit to 1 on successful completion of any FP
43:  *       instruction.
44:  *     FPCCR.LSPEN:  Enables lazy context save of FP state. When this is
45:  *       done, the processor reserves space on the stack for the FP state,
46:  *       but does not save that state information to the stack.
47:  *
48:  *  Software must not change the value of the ASPEN bit or LSPEN bit while
49:  *  either:
50:  *
51:  *   - the CPACR permits access to CP10 and CP11, that give access to the FP
52:  *     extension, or
53:  *   - the CONTROL.FPCA bit is set to 1
54:  *
55:  ****************************************************************************/
56: 
57: void arm_fpuconfig(void)
58: {
59:   uint32_t regval;
60: 
61:   /* Set CONTROL.FPCA so that we always get the extended context frame
62:    * with the volatile FP registers stacked above the basic context.
63:    */
64: 
65:   regval = getcontrol();
66:   regval |= CONTROL_FPCA;
67:   setcontrol(regval);
68: 
69:   /* Ensure that FPCCR.LSPEN is disabled, so that we don't have to contend
70:    * with the lazy FP context save behavior.  Clear FPCCR.ASPEN since we
71:    * are going to turn on CONTROL.FPCA for all contexts.
72:    */
73: 
74:   regval = getreg32(NVIC_FPCCR);
75:   regval &= ~(NVIC_FPCCR_ASPEN | NVIC_FPCCR_LSPEN);
76:   putreg32(regval, NVIC_FPCCR);
77: 
78:   /* Enable full access to CP10 and CP11 */
79: 
80:   regval = getreg32(NVIC_CPACR);
81:   regval |= NVIC_CPACR_CP_FULL(10) | NVIC_CPACR_CP_FULL(11);
82:   putreg32(regval, NVIC_CPACR);
83: }

137: /****************************************************************************
138:  * Name: spin_lock_notrace
139:  *
140:  * Description:
141:  *   If this CPU does not already hold the spinlock, then loop until the
142:  *   spinlock is successfully locked.
143:  *
144:  *   This implementation is the same as the above spin_lock() except that
145:  *   it does not perform instrumentation logic.
146:  *
147:  * Input Parameters:
148:  *   lock - A reference to the spinlock object to lock.
149:  *
150:  * Returned Value:
151:  *   None.  When the function returns, the spinlock was successfully locked
152:  *   by this CPU.
153:  *
154:  * Assumptions:
155:  *   Not running at the interrupt level.
156:  *
157:  ****************************************************************************/
158: 
159: #ifdef CONFIG_SPINLOCK
160: static inline_function noinstrument_function
161: void spin_lock_notrace(FAR volatile spinlock_t *lock)
162: {
163: #ifdef CONFIG_TICKET_SPINLOCK
164:   int ticket = atomic_add_relaxed(&lock->next, 1);
165:   while (atomic_read_acquire(&lock->owner) != ticket);
166: #else /* CONFIG_TICKET_SPINLOCK */
167:   while (atomic_xchg_acquire(&lock->lock, 1) == 1);
168: #endif
169: }
170: #else
171: #  define spin_lock_notrace(lock) ((void)(lock))
172: #endif /* CONFIG_SPINLOCK */
173: 
174: /****************************************************************************
175:  * Name: spin_lock
176:  *
177:  * Description:
178:  *   If this CPU does not already hold the spinlock, then loop until the
179:  *   spinlock is successfully locked.
180:  *
181:  *   This implementation is non-reentrant and is prone to deadlocks in
182:  *   the case that any logic on the same CPU attempts to take the lock
183:  *   more than once.
184:  *
185:  * Input Parameters:
186:  *   lock - A reference to the spinlock object to lock.
187:  *
188:  * Returned Value:
189:  *   None.  When the function returns, the spinlock was successfully locked
190:  *   by this CPU.
191:  *
192:  * Assumptions:
193:  *   Not running at the interrupt level.
194:  *
195:  ****************************************************************************/
196: 
197: #ifdef CONFIG_SPINLOCK
198: static inline_function void spin_lock(FAR volatile spinlock_t *lock)
199: {
200:   /* Mark that we want to hold lock */
201: 
202:   spinlock_mark_locking(&lock->info);
203: 
204:   /* Notify that we are waiting for a spinlock */
205: 
206:   sched_note_spinlock(lock, NOTE_SPINLOCK_LOCK);
207: 
208:   /* If CONFIG_SCHED_CRITMONITOR_MAXTIME_BUSYWAIT >= 0, count busy-waiting. */
209: 
210:   nxsched_critmon_busywait(true, return_address(0));
211: 
212:   /* Lock without trace note */
213: 
214:   spin_lock_notrace(lock);
215: 
216:   /* Mark the spinlock has been locked */
217: 
218:   spinlock_mark_locked(&lock->info);
219: 
220:   /* Get the lock, end counting busy-waiting */
221: 
222:   nxsched_critmon_busywait(false, return_address(0));
223: 
224:   /* Notify that we have the spinlock */
225: 
226:   sched_note_spinlock(lock, NOTE_SPINLOCK_LOCKED);
227: }
228: #else
229: #  define spin_lock(lock) ((void)(lock))
230: #endif /* CONFIG_SPINLOCK */

232: /****************************************************************************
233:  * Name: spin_trylock_notrace
234:  *
235:  * Description:
236:  *   Try once to lock the spinlock.  Do not wait if the spinlock is already
237:  *   locked.
238:  *
239:  *   This implementation is the same as the above spin_trylock() except that
240:  *   it does not perform instrumentation logic.
241:  *
242:  * Input Parameters:
243:  *   lock - A reference to the spinlock object to lock.
244:  *
245:  * Returned Value:
246:  *   false - Failure, the spinlock was already locked
247:  *   true  - Success, the spinlock was successfully locked
248:  *
249:  * Assumptions:
250:  *   Not running at the interrupt level.
251:  *
252:  ****************************************************************************/
253: 
254: #ifdef CONFIG_SPINLOCK
255: static inline_function noinstrument_function bool
256: spin_trylock_notrace(FAR volatile spinlock_t *lock)
257: {
258: #ifdef CONFIG_TICKET_SPINLOCK
259:   atomic_t expected = atomic_read(&lock->owner);
260:   atomic_t next = expected + 1;
261: 
262:   /* Keep the expected value private.  A failed compare-exchange updates its
263:    * expected argument; passing &lock->owner would corrupt the ticket owner. */
264:   return atomic_cmpxchg_acquire(&lock->next, &expected, next);
265: #else /* CONFIG_TICKET_SPINLOCK */
266:   return atomic_xchg_acquire(&lock->lock, 1) != 1;
267: #endif /* CONFIG_TICKET_SPINLOCK */
268: }
269: #else
270: #  define spin_trylock_notrace(lock) ((void)(lock), true)
271: #endif /* CONFIG_SPINLOCK */
272: 
273: /****************************************************************************
274:  * Name: spin_trylock
275:  *
276:  * Description:
277:  *   Try once to lock the spinlock.  Do not wait if the spinlock is already
278:  *   locked.
279:  *
280:  * Input Parameters:
281:  *   lock - A reference to the spinlock object to lock.
282:  *
283:  * Returned Value:
284:  *   false - Failure, the spinlock was already locked
285:  *   true  - Success, the spinlock was successfully locked
286:  *
287:  * Assumptions:
288:  *   Not running at the interrupt level.
289:  *
290:  ****************************************************************************/
291: 
292: #ifdef CONFIG_SPINLOCK
293: static inline_function bool spin_trylock(FAR volatile spinlock_t *lock)
294: {
295:   bool locked;
296: 
297:   /* Notify that we are waiting for a spinlock */
298: 
299:   sched_note_spinlock(lock, NOTE_SPINLOCK_LOCK);
300: 
301:   /* Try lock without trace note */
302: 
303:   locked = spin_trylock_notrace(lock);
304:   if (locked)
305:     {
306:       /* Mark the spinlock has been locked */
307: 
308:       spinlock_mark_locked(&lock->info);
309: 
310:       /* Notify that we have the spinlock */
311: 
312:       sched_note_spinlock(lock, NOTE_SPINLOCK_LOCKED);
313:     }
314:   else
315:     {
316:       /* Notify that we abort for a spinlock */
317: 
318:       sched_note_spinlock(lock, NOTE_SPINLOCK_ABORT);
319:     }
320: 
321:   return locked;
322: }
323: #else
324: #  define spin_trylock(lock) ((void)(lock), true)
325: #endif /* CONFIG_SPINLOCK */

330:  * Description:
331:  *   Release one count on a non-reentrant spinlock.

334:  *   it does not perform instrumentation logic.

336:  * Input Parameters:

343:  *   Not running at the interrupt level.

345:  ****************************************************************************/

347: #ifdef CONFIG_SPINLOCK
348: static inline_function noinstrument_function void
349: spin_unlock_notrace(FAR volatile spinlock_t *lock)

351: #ifdef CONFIG_TICKET_SPINLOCK

353: #else

641:  * Name: rspin_lock/rspin_lock_irqsave/rspin_lock_irqsave_nopreempt
642:  *
643:  * Description:
644:  *   Nest supported spinlock, can support UINT16_MAX max depth.
645:  *   As we should not disable irq for long time, sched also locked.
646:  *   Similar feature with enter_critical_section, but isolate by instance.
647:  *
648:  *   If SPINLOCK is enabled:
649:  *     Will take spinlock each cpu first call.
650:  *
651:  *   If SPINLOCK is not enabled:
652:  *     Equivalent to up_irq_save() + sched_lock().
653:  *     Will only sched_lock once when first called.
654:  *
655:  *   NOTE: This function is only allowed to execute with irq disabled.
656:  *
657:  * Input Parameters:
658:  *   lock - Caller specific rspinlock_s. not NULL.
659:  *
660:  * Returned Value:
661:  *   An opaque, architecture-specific value that represents the state of
662:  *   the interrupts prior to the call to spin_lock_irqsave(lock);
663:  *
664:  ****************************************************************************/
665: 
666: #ifdef CONFIG_SPINLOCK
667: static inline_function
668: void rspin_lock(FAR rspinlock_t *lock)
669: {
670:   rspinlock_t new_val;
671:   rspinlock_t old_val;
672:   int         cpu = this_cpu() + 1;
673: 
674:   /* Already owned this lock. */
675: 
676:   old_val.val = atomic_read(&lock->val);
677: 
678:   if (old_val.owner == cpu)
679:     {
680:       lock->count += 1;
681:     }
682:   else
683:     {
684:       /* Mark that we want to hold lock */
685: 
686:       spinlock_mark_locking(&lock->info);
687: 
688:       /* Try seize the ownership of the lock using CAS. */
689: 
690:       new_val.count = 1;
691:       new_val.owner = cpu;
692: 
693:       do
694:         {
695:           old_val.val = 0;
696:         }
697:       while (!atomic_cmpxchg_acquire(&lock->val,
698:              &old_val.val, new_val.val));
699: 
700:       /* Mark locked only when the lock is acquired for the first time. */
701: 
702:       spinlock_mark_locked(&lock->info);
703:     }
704: }

706: static inline_function
707: irqstate_t rspin_lock_irqsave(FAR rspinlock_t *lock)
708: {
709:   irqstate_t flags = up_irq_save();
710:   rspin_lock(lock);
711: 
712:   return flags;
713: }
714: #else
715: static inline_function
716: irqstate_t rspin_lock_irqsave(FAR rspinlock_t *lock)
717: {
718:   irqstate_t flags = up_irq_save();
719:   lock->count++;
720:   lock->owner = this_cpu() + 1;
721:   return flags;
722: }
723: #endif

727: {
728:   irqstate_t flags;
729:   flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(lock);
730:   sched_lock();
731:   return flags;

151:       /* Perform the semaphore unlock operation, releasing this task as a

153:        *
154:        * NOTE:  When semaphores are used for signaling purposes, the holder
155:        * of the semaphore may not be this thread!  In this case,
156:        * nxsem_release_holder() will do nothing.
157:        *
158:        * In the case of a mutex this could be simply resolved since there is
159:        * only one holder but for the case of counting semaphores, there may
160:        * be many holders and if the holder is not this thread, then it is
161:        * not possible to know which thread/holder should be released.
162:        *
163:        * For this reason, it is recommended that priority inheritance be
164:        * disabled via nxsem_set_protocol(SEM_PRIO_NONE) when the semaphore is
165:        * initialized if the semaphore is to used for signaling purposes.
166:        */
167: 
168:       if (!mutex || blocking)
169:         {
170:           nxsem_release_holder(sem);
171:         }
172: 
173: #if defined(CONFIG_PRIORITY_INHERITANCE) || defined(CONFIG_PRIORITY_PROTECT)
174:       /* Don't let any unblocked tasks run until we complete any priority
175:        * restoration steps.  Interrupts are disabled, but we do not want
176:        * the head of the ready-to-run list to be modified yet.
177:        *
178:        * NOTE: If this sched_lock is called from an interrupt handler, it
179:        * will do nothing.
180:        */
181: 
182:       proto = sem->flags & SEM_PRIO_MASK;
183:       if (proto != SEM_PRIO_NONE)
184:         {
185:           sched_lock();
186:         }
187: #endif
188: 
189:       /* If the result of semaphore unlock is non-positive, then
190:        * there must be some task waiting for the semaphore.
191:        */
192: 
193:       if (blocking)
194:         {
195:           /* Check if there are any tasks in the waiting for semaphore
196:            * task list that are waiting for this semaphore.  This is a
197:            * prioritized list so the first one we encounter is the one
198:            * that we want.
199:            */
200: 
201:           stcb = (FAR struct tcb_s *)dq_remfirst(SEM_WAITLIST(sem));
202:           if (stcb != NULL)
203:             {
204:               FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
205: 
206:               /* The task will be the new holder of the semaphore when
207:                * it is awakened.
208:                */
209: 
210:               if (mutex)
211:                 {
212:                   int32_t blocking_bit = dq_empty(SEM_WAITLIST(sem)) ?
213:                     0 : NXSEM_MBLOCKING_BIT;
214:                   atomic_set(NXSEM_MHOLDER(sem), stcb->pid | blocking_bit);
215:                 }
216:               else
217:                 {
218:                   nxsem_add_holder_tcb(stcb, sem);

223:               wd_cancel(&stcb->waitdog);

43:  * Description:
44:  *    This function is used to process the tcb in g_delivertasks.
45:  * 1 We use direct locking instead of enter_critical_section
46:  * to save processing time
47:  * 2 If there is a higher priority task, we will still perform
48:  * the higher priority task
49:  * 3 If the schedule lock is on, the task will be placed in g_pendingtasks

53:  *
54:  * Returned Value:
55:  *   OK

58:  * - The caller must be in irq
59:  * - current cpu must not be locked
60:  *
61:  ****************************************************************************/
62: 
63: void nxsched_process_delivered(int cpu)
64: {
65:   enum task_deliver_e priority;
66:   irqstate_t flags;
67: 
68:   DEBUGASSERT(up_interrupt_context());
69: 
70:   flags = enter_critical_section();
71:   priority = per_cpu_var_smp(g_delivertasks, cpu);
72:   per_cpu_var_smp(g_delivertasks, cpu) = SWITCH_NONE;
73: 
74:   if (priority != SWITCH_NONE &&
75:       !nxsched_switch_running(cpu, priority == SWITCH_EQUAL))
76:     {
77:       /* Manage the (rare) case that task delivery to this CPU was not
78:        * successful. This can happen in two cases:
79:        * 1) The currently running task on this CPU just entered sched_lock
80:        * 2) This CPU just picked a higher priority task to execute
81:        *    before this SMP call was executed
82:        * To avoid schedule latency/priority inversion, just check once more
83:        * if there is another CPU eglible to run the delivered task, and
84:        * pass it forward.
85:        */
86: 
87:       FAR struct tcb_s *tcb = (FAR struct tcb_s *)dq_peek(list_readytorun());
88:       if (tcb)
89:         {
90:           int target_cpu = tcb->flags & TCB_FLAG_CPU_LOCKED ?
91:             tcb->cpu : nxsched_select_cpu(tcb->affinity);
92:           if (target_cpu != cpu &&
93:               current_task(target_cpu)->sched_priority < tcb->sched_priority)
94:             {
95:               nxsched_deliver_task(cpu, target_cpu, priority);
96:             }
97:         }
98:     }
99: 
100:   leave_critical_section(flags);

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * BK7258 AP_SPINLOCK-backed software hwspinlock.
3:  ****************************************************************************/
4: 
5: #include <nuttx/config.h>
6: 
7: #include <assert.h>
8: #include <stdbool.h>
9: #include <stdint.h>
10: 
11: #include <nuttx/hwspinlock/hwspinlock.h>
12: 
13: #include "arm_internal.h"
14: #include "bk7258_boottrace.h"
15: 
16: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ENTRY       0xa1000000u
17: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_REENTER     0xa2000000u
18: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_OWNER_BUSY  0xa3000000u
19: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_INTENT      0xa4000000u
20: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_CONFLICT    0xa5000000u
21: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ACQUIRED    0xa6000000u
22: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_UNLOCK      0xa7000000u
23: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_RELEASED    0xa8000000u
24: 
25: struct bk7258_atomic_gate_s
26: {
27:   volatile uint32_t interested[2];
28:   volatile uint32_t turn;
29:   volatile uint32_t owner;
30:   volatile uint32_t depth;
31: };
32: 
33: static struct bk7258_atomic_gate_s g_bk7258_atomic_gate
34:   __attribute__((section(".bk_spinlock"), aligned(32)));
35: 
36: static inline void bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(unsigned int cpu, uint32_t value)
37: {
38:   if (cpu == 0 &&
39:       bk7258_boottrace_primary_stage() == BK7258_BOOT_CPU2_FIRST_IRQ)
40:     {
41:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(4, value);
42:     }
43: }
44: 
45: static bool bk7258_hwspinlock_trylock(struct hwspinlock_dev_s *dev)
46: {
47:   unsigned int cpu = (unsigned int)up_cpu_index();
48:   unsigned int other = cpu ^ 1u;
49: 
50:   (void)dev;
51:   DEBUGASSERT(cpu < 2);
52:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ENTRY);
53: 
54:   /* BK7258 has only two SRAM exclusive monitors while CP, AP CPU1 and AP
55:    * CPU2 are all active.  Keep the AP-only atomic gate independent of
56:    * LDAEX/STREX so CP traffic cannot starve an AP exclusive sequence.
57:    */
58: 
59:   /* libc atomics are normally short, but the scheduler's recursive critical
60:    * section can issue another atomic operation on the same CPU.  Re-entry
61:    * must be decided before entering Peterson arbitration; otherwise a waiter
62:    * on the other CPU can make the current owner wait for itself.
63:    */
64: 
65:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner == cpu + 1u)
66:     {
67:       if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth == UINT32_MAX)
68:         {
69:           PANIC();
70:         }
71: 
72:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth++;
73:       UP_DMB();
74:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_REENTER |
75:                              g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth);
76:       return true;
77:     }
78: 
79:   /* This is only a fast rejection.  The Peterson protocol below remains
80:    * authoritative while a new owner is between intent and owner publish.
81:    */
82: 
83:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner != 0)
84:     {
85:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_OWNER_BUSY |
86:                              g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner);
87:       return false;
88:     }
89: 
90:   /* Every attempt must publish a fresh intent and turn.  Leaving intent set
91:    * after a failed trylock makes the state stale and breaks trylock's
92:    * one-attempt contract.
93:    */
94: 
95:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[cpu] = 1;
96:   UP_DMB();
97:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.turn = other;
98:   UP_DMB();
99:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_INTENT);
100: 
101:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[other] != 0 &&
102:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.turn == other)
103:     {
104:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[cpu] = 0;
105:       UP_DMB();
106:       __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
107:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_CONFLICT);
108:       return false;
109:     }
110: 
111:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner = cpu + 1u;
112:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth = 1;
113:   UP_DMB();
114:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ACQUIRED);
115:   return true;
116: }
117: 
118: static void bk7258_hwspinlock_relax(struct hwspinlock_dev_s *dev)
119: {
120:   (void)dev;
121:   __asm__ volatile("nop" ::: "memory");
122: }
123: 
124: static void bk7258_hwspinlock_unlock(struct hwspinlock_dev_s *dev)
125: {
126:   unsigned int cpu = (unsigned int)up_cpu_index();
127: 
128:   (void)dev;
129:   if (cpu >= 2 || g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner != cpu + 1u ||
130:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth == 0)
131:     {
132:       PANIC();
133:     }
134: 
135:   if (--g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth != 0)
136:     {
137:       UP_DMB();
138:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_UNLOCK |
139:                              g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth);
140:       return;
141:     }
142: 
143:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner = 0;
144:   UP_DMB();
145:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[cpu] = 0;
146:   UP_DSB();
147:   __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
148:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_RELEASED);
149: }
150: 
151: const struct hwspinlock_ops_s g_bk7258_hwspinlock_ops =
152: {
153:   .trylock = bk7258_hwspinlock_trylock,
154:   .relax   = bk7258_hwspinlock_relax,
155:   .unlock  = bk7258_hwspinlock_unlock
156: };
157: 
158: void bk7258_hwspinlock_initialize(void)
159: {
160:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[0] = 0;
161:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[1] = 0;
162:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.turn = 0;
163:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner = 0;
164:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth = 0;
165:   UP_DSB();
166:   __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
167: }

212: /****************************************************************************
213:  * Name:  nxsched_add_readytorun
214:  *
215:  * Description:
216:  *   This function adds a TCB to one of the ready to run lists. The list
217:  *   will be:
218:  *
219:  *   1. The g_readytorun list if the task is ready-to-run but not running
220:  *      and not assigned to a CPU.
221:  *   2. The g_assignedtask[cpu] list if the task is running or if has been
222:  *      assigned to a CPU.
223:  *
224:  *   If the currently active task has preemption disabled and the new TCB
225:  *   would cause this task to be pre-empted, the new task is added to the
226:  *   g_pendingtasks list instead.  The pending tasks will be made
227:  *   ready-to-run when preemption isunlocked.
228:  *
229:  * Input Parameters:
230:  *   btcb - Points to the blocked TCB that is ready-to-run
231:  *
232:  * Returned Value:
233:  *   true if the currently active task (the head of the ready-to-run list)
234:  *   has changed.
235:  *
236:  * Assumptions:
237:  * - The caller has established a critical section before calling this
238:  *   function (calling sched_lock() first is NOT a good idea -- use
239:  *   enter_critical_section()).
240:  * - The caller has already removed the input rtcb from whatever list it
241:  *   was in.
242:  * - The caller handles the condition that occurs if the head of the
243:  *   ready-to-run list has changed.
244:  *
245:  ****************************************************************************/
246: 
247: bool nxsched_add_readytorun(FAR struct tcb_s *btcb)
248: {
249:   bool doswitch = false;
250:   int target_cpu = btcb->flags & TCB_FLAG_CPU_LOCKED ? btcb->cpu :
251:     nxsched_select_cpu(btcb->affinity);
252:   FAR struct tcb_s *tcb = current_task(target_cpu);
253: 
254:   /* Add the btcb to the ready to run list, and try to run it on the target
255:    * CPU
256:    */
257: 
258:   btcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_READYTORUN;
259:   nxsched_add_prioritized(btcb, list_readytorun());
260: 
261:   /* In some cases, such as setaffinity, cpu need to be used. */
262: 
263:   btcb->cpu = target_cpu;
264:   if (tcb->sched_priority < btcb->sched_priority)
265:     {
266:       doswitch = nxsched_deliver_task(this_cpu(), target_cpu,
267:                                       SWITCH_HIGHER);
268:     }
269: 
270:   return doswitch;
271: }
272: 
273: #endif /* CONFIG_SMP */

412:  *     this function is called on each timer interrupt and a value of one
413:  *     is implicit.

454:         }

457:     }

460: }

120:  * Name:  nxsched_switch_running
121:  *
122:  * Description:
123:  *   This function switches the head of the current CPU's assigned tasks
124:  *   list to the TCB given as parameter. The idle task is not switched out.
125:  *   If the running task can't be swapped out, the btcb is pushed to
126:  *   the ready-to-run list.
127:  *
128:  * Input Parameters:
129:  *   cpu          - Always this_cpu(). Given as argument only for
130:  *                  optimization
131:  *   switch_equal - When true, switch away a task of equal priority compared
132:  *                  to the pending one
133:  *
134:  * Returned Value:
135:  *   true if the currently active task is switched
136:  *
137:  * Assumptions:
138:  * - The caller has established a critical section
139:  * - The caller has already removed the input rtcb from whatever list it
140:  *   was in.
141:  * - The caller handles the condition that occurs if the head of the
142:  *   assigned tasks list has changed.
143:  *
144:  ****************************************************************************/
145: 
146: bool nxsched_switch_running(int cpu, bool switch_equal)
147: {
148:   FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = current_task(cpu);
149:   int sched_priority = rtcb->sched_priority;
150:   FAR struct tcb_s *btcb;
151:   bool ret = false;
152: 
153:   DEBUGASSERT(cpu == this_cpu());
154: 
155:   if (nxsched_islocked_tcb(rtcb))
156:     {
157:       return false;
158:     }
159: 
160:   if (switch_equal && sched_priority > 0)
161:     {
162:       sched_priority--;
163:     }
164: 
165:   /* If there is a task in readytorun list, which is eglible to run on this
166:    * CPU, and has higher priority than the current task,
167:    * switch the current task to that one.
168:    */
169: 
170:   for (btcb = (FAR struct tcb_s *)dq_peek(list_readytorun());
171:        btcb && btcb->sched_priority > sched_priority;
172:        btcb = btcb->flink)
173:     {
174:       /* Check if the task found in ready-to-run list is allowed to run on
175:        * this CPU. TCB_FLAG_CPU_LOCKED may be used to override affinity. If
176:        * the flag is set, assume that btcb->cpu is valid, and it is the only
177:        * CPU on which the btcb can run.
178:        */
179: 
180:       if (CPU_ISSET(cpu, &btcb->affinity) &&
181:           ((btcb->flags & TCB_FLAG_CPU_LOCKED) == 0 || btcb->cpu == cpu))
182:         {
183:           /* Found a task, remove it from ready-to-run list */
184: 
185:           dq_rem((FAR struct dq_entry_s *)btcb, list_readytorun());
186: 
187:           if (!is_idle_task(rtcb))
188:             {
189:               /* Put currently running task back to ready-to-run list */
190: 
191:               rtcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_READYTORUN;

133:   clock_t ret;
134:   int decr;
135: 
136:   /* How much can we decrement the timeslice delay?  If 'ticks' is greater
137:    * than the timeslice value, then we ignore any excess amount.
138:    *
139:    * 'ticks' should not be greater than the remaining timeslice.  But that
140:    * event seems to be possible, perhaps in cases where pre-emption has been
141:    * disabled or the noswitches flag is set.  This might cause jitter of a
142:    * few ticks in the slicing because the excess amount is not handled.
143:    */
144: 
145:   DEBUGASSERT(tcb != NULL);
146:   decr = MIN(tcb->timeslice, ticks);

148:   /* Decrement the timeslice counter */
149: 
150:   tcb->timeslice -= decr;
151: 
152:   /* Did decrementing the timeslice counter cause the timeslice to expire? */
153: 
154:   ret = tcb->timeslice;
155:   if (tcb->timeslice <= 0 && !nxsched_islocked_tcb(tcb))
156:     {

160:        * as soon as possible and we can perform this action in the normal
161:        * timer expiration context.

164:        * that the situation is impossible or at least could only occur on
165:        * rare corner-cases.
166:        */
167: 
168:       if (noswitches)
169:         {
170:           ret = 0;
171:         }
172:       else
173:         {
174:           /* Reset the timeslice. */
175: 
176:           tcb->timeslice = MSEC2TICK(CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL);
177:           ret = tcb->timeslice;
178: 
179:           /* We know we are at the head of the ready to run prioritized
180:            * list.  We must be the highest priority task eligible for
181:            * execution.  Check the next task in the ready to run list.  If
182:            * it is the same priority, then we need to relinquish the CPU and
183:            * give that task a shot.
184:            */

187:           ptcb = (FAR struct tcb_s *)dq_peek(list_readytorun());

190: #endif
191:           if (ptcb &&

193:             {
194:               FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
195: 
196:               /* Just resetting the task priority to its current value.
197:                * This will cause the task to be rescheduled behind any
198:                * other tasks at the same priority.
199:                */

201: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
202:               DEBUGASSERT(tcb->task_state == TSTATE_TASK_RUNNING);

206:                                         nxsched_roundrobin_handler,

208:                   nxsched_smp_call_single_async(tcb->cpu, &g_call_data);

40:  * operation is a not a normal branch operation and instead, that the
41:  * exception is complete. Therefore, it starts the exception return sequence.
42:  *

44:  * eventual processor mode.
45:  * The remaining bits of the EXC_RETURN value should be set to 1.
46:  */

42: /****************************************************************************
43:  * Name: nxsched_set_affinity
44:  *
45:  * Description:
46:  *   sched_setaffinity() sets the CPU affinity mask of the thread whose ID
47:  *   is pid to the value specified by mask.  If pid is zero, then the
48:  *   calling thread is used.  The argument cpusetsize is the length (i
49:  *   bytes) of the data pointed to by mask.  Normally this argument would
50:  *   be specified as sizeof(cpu_set_t).
51:  *
52:  *   If the thread specified by pid is not currently running on one of the
53:  *   CPUs specified in mask, then that thread is migrated to one of the
54:  *   CPUs specified in mask.
55:  *
56:  *   nxsched_set_affinity() is identical to the function sched_setparam(),
57:  *   differing only in its return value:  This function does not modify
58:  *   the errno variable.  This is a non-standard, internal OS function and
59:  *   is not intended for use by application logic.  Applications should
60:  *   use the standard sched_setparam().
61:  *
62:  * Input Parameters:
63:  *   pid        - The ID of thread whose affinity set will be modified.
64:  *   cpusetsize - Size of mask.  MUST be sizeofcpu_set_t().
65:  *   mask       - The location to return the thread's new affinity set.
66:  *
67:  * Returned Value:
68:  *   Zero (OK) if successful.  Otherwise, a negated errno value is returned:
69:  *
70:  *     ESRCH  The task whose ID is pid could not be found.
71:  *
72:  ****************************************************************************/
73: 
74: int nxsched_set_affinity(pid_t pid, size_t cpusetsize,
75:                          FAR const cpu_set_t *mask)
76: {
77:   FAR struct tcb_s *tcb;
78:   irqstate_t flags;
79:   int ret = OK;
80: 
81:   DEBUGASSERT(cpusetsize == sizeof(cpu_set_t) && mask != NULL);
82: 
83:   /* Make sure that affinity mask is valid */
84: 
85:   if (*mask == 0)
86:     {
87:       return -EINVAL;
88:     }
89: 
90:   /* Verify that the PID corresponds to a real task */
91: 
92:   if (!pid)
93:     {
94:       tcb = this_task();
95:     }
96:   else
97:     {
98:       tcb = nxsched_get_tcb(pid);
99:     }
100: 
101:   if (tcb == NULL)
102:     {
103:       ret = -ESRCH;
104:       goto errout;
105:     }
106: 
107:   /* Don't permit changing the affinity mask of any task locked to a CPU
108:    * (i.e., an IDLE task)
109:    */
110: 
111:   flags = enter_critical_section();
112:   if ((atomic_read(&tcb->flags) & TCB_FLAG_CPU_LOCKED) != 0)
113:     {
114:       ret = -EINVAL;
115:       goto errout_with_csection;
116:     }
117: 
118:   /* Set the new affinity mask. */
119: 
120:   tcb->affinity = *mask;
121: 
122:   /* Is the task still executing a a CPU in its affinity mask? Will this
123:    * change cause the task to be removed from its current assigned task
124:    * list?
125:    *
126:    * First... is the task in an assigned task list?
127:    */
128: 
129:   if (tcb->task_state >= FIRST_READY_TO_RUN_STATE &&
130:       tcb->task_state <= LAST_READY_TO_RUN_STATE)
131:     {
132:       /* Yes... is the CPU associated with the assigned task in the new
133:        * affinity mask?
134:        */
135: 
136:       if ((tcb->affinity & (1 << tcb->cpu)) == 0)
137:         {
138:           /* No.. then we will need to move the task from the assigned
139:            * task list to some other ready to run list.
140:            *
141:            * nxsched_set_priority() will do just what we want... it will
142:            * remove the task from its current position in the some assigned
143:            * task list and then simply put it back in the right place.  This
144:            * works even if the task is this task.
145:            */
146: 
147:           ret = nxsched_set_priority(tcb, tcb->sched_priority);
148:         }
149:     }
150: 
151: errout_with_csection:
152:   leave_critical_section(flags);
153:   if (pid)
154:     {
155:       nxsched_put_tcb(tcb);
156:     }
157: 
158: errout:
159:   return ret;
160: }

168:  *   calling thread is used.  The argument cpusetsize is the length (i
169:  *   bytes) of the data pointed to by mask.  Normally this argument would
170:  *   be specified as sizeof(cpu_set_t).
171:  *
172:  *   If the thread specified by pid is not currently running on one of the
173:  *   CPUs specified in mask, then that thread is migrated to one of the
174:  *   CPUs specified in mask.
175:  *
176:  *   This function is a simply wrapper around nxsched_set_affinity() that
177:  *   sets the errno value in the event of an error.
178:  *
179:  * Input Parameters:

181:  *   cpusetsize - Size of mask.  MUST be sizeofcpu_set_t().
182:  *   mask       - The location to return the thread's new affinity set.
183:  *
184:  * Returned Value:
185:  *   0 if successful.  Otherwise, ERROR (-1) is returned, and errno is
186:  *   set appropriately:
187:  *
188:  *     ESRCH  The task whose ID is pid could not be found.
189:  *
190:  ****************************************************************************/
191:

193:                       FAR const cpu_set_t *mask)
194: {
195:   int ret = nxsched_set_affinity(pid, cpusetsize, mask);

76:         irq    -= NVIC_IRQ_FIRST;

30: /****************************************************************************
31:  * Pre-processor Prototypes
32:  ****************************************************************************/
33: 
34: /* In the normal cases, interrupts are not nest-able and all interrupts run
35:  * at an execution priority between NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_MIN and
36:  * NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_MAX (with NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_MAX reserved for SVCall).
37:  *
38:  * If, in addition, CONFIG_ARCH_HIPRI_INTERRUPT is defined, then special
39:  * high priority interrupts are supported.  These are not "nested" in the
40:  * normal sense of the word.  These high priority interrupts can interrupt
41:  * normal processing but execute outside of OS (although they can "get back
42:  * into the game" via a PendSV interrupt).
43:  *
44:  * In the normal course of things, interrupts must occasionally be disabled
45:  * using the up_irq_save() inline function to prevent contention in use of
46:  * resources that may be shared between interrupt level and non-interrupt
47:  * level logic.  Now the question arises, if we are using
48:  * CONFIG_ARCH_HIPRI_INTERRUPT=y, do we disable all interrupts except
49:  * SVCall (we cannot disable SVCall interrupts).  Or do we only disable the
50:  * "normal" interrupts?
51:  *
52:  * If we are using the BASEPRI register to disable interrupts, then the
53:  * answer is that we must disable ONLY the "normal interrupts".  That
54:  * is because we cannot disable SVCALL interrupts and we cannot permit
55:  * SVCAll interrupts running at a higher priority than the high priority
56:  * interrupts (otherwise, they will introduce jitter in the high priority
57:  * interrupt response time.)
58:  *
59:  * Hence, if you need to disable the high priority interrupt, you will have
60:  * to disable the interrupt either at the peripheral that generates the
61:  * interrupt or at the NVIC.  Disabling global interrupts via the BASEPRI
62:  * register cannot effect high priority interrupts.
63:  */
64: 
65: /* The high priority interrupt must be highest priority.  This prevents
66:  * SVCALL handling from adding jitter to high priority interrupt response.
67:  * Disabling interrupts will disable all interrupts EXCEPT SVCALL and the
68:  * high priority interrupts.
69:  */
70: 
71: #define NVIC_SYSH_MAXNORMAL_PRIORITY  NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_DEFAULT
72: #define NVIC_SYSH_HIGH_PRIORITY       (NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_DEFAULT - 2*NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_STEP)
73: #define NVIC_SYSH_DISABLE_PRIORITY    NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_DEFAULT
74: #define NVIC_SYSH_SVCALL_PRIORITY     (NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_DEFAULT - 1*NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_STEP)

The strongest conclusion is that enabling SysTick is coupled to two independent readiness hazards: a stale-pending exception can preempt immediately, and the high-priority TX worker can post readiness yet prevent the lower-priority bring-up thread from ever observing it. The atomic gate, PendSV/FPU frame, and scheduling IPI issues are real secondary risks, but the current evidence does not put them ahead of those two.
